html:
In Operation Priboi, from 25 to 28 March 1949, the Soviet authorities deported about 90,000 people from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to Siberia. Around 42,000 of them were from Latvia.

Most were farm families labelled kulaks, rich peasants, or relatives of the Forest Brothers partisans. Many were women, children and the elderly. They were taken in cattle wagons to remote settlements, where many died. Survivors could return only after Stalin's death, and some never did.

The aim was to crush resistance to collective farms, and it worked: within months nearly all farms in the Baltic were collectivised. The deportation followed those of June 1941 and is a central memory in Latvia and its neighbours, under the Soviet Union.
